source.name: ECDC – European Respiratory Virus Surveillance Summary (ERVISS)
source.publisher: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), an EU agency
source.note: Figures are reported every week by the national public health institutes (FHI, Folkhälsomyndigheten, SSI and THL) to ECDC, which publishes them openly every Friday. Recent weeks can be revised.

findings: Norway had 387 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 45, up 8% on the week before. That is 12% of an average season peak (low intensity).
Sweden had 126 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 45, up 12% on the week before. That is 5% of an average season peak (baseline intensity).
Denmark had 125 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 45, down 11% on the week before. That is 5% of an average season peak (baseline intensity).
Finland had 70 lab-confirmed influenza cases in week 45, down 23% on the week before. That is 6% of an average season peak (baseline intensity).
Norway has the most influenza relative to a normal season: 12% of an average season peak.
A(H1N1)pdm09 accounts for 88% of subtyped influenza samples this season, across the Nordic countries.
COVID-19 cases this week: Norway 299 (+15%, low); Sweden 176 (+32%, baseline); Denmark 84 (−15%, baseline); Finland 35 (−42%, baseline).
RSV cases this week: Norway 16 (+23%, baseline); Sweden 3 (−25%, baseline); Denmark 0 (−100%, baseline); Finland 9 (+125%, baseline).
Sweden reported 0 deaths with influenza and 5 deaths with COVID-19 and Denmark reported 8.2 hospitalisations for severe respiratory infection (SARI) this week.
headline: The Nordics had 708 lab-confirmed influenza cases this week, about the same as last week. That is 10% of an average season peak (baseline intensity).
Other viruses: COVID-19 594 (flat, baseline).
key_points: Norway has the most influenza relative to a normal season: 12% of an average season peak.

source.name: WHO FluNet – Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS)
source.note: Weekly influenza tests and positives reported by each country's National Influenza Centre to WHO. Recent weeks are often incomplete and are revised.

points: Australia's 2026 flu season has stayed below 10% test positivity: 8.5% in week 45, with a high of 9.6% in week 39, 44% of an average peak (medium intensity). It came late: positivity usually passes 10% around week 24. A(H3N2) made up 47% of subtyped samples.
Intensity of the other southern-hemisphere seasons: New Zealand very high, Chile very high and South Africa high.
Main virus in the southern-hemisphere winter, an early hint of what the Nordics may see: A(H3N2) in Australia, A(H1N1)pdm09 in New Zealand, B in Chile and A(H3N2) in South Africa.
Influenza positivity is already above 10% in Japan (since week 40) and England (since week 43), but not yet in the United States or Canada.
